title: Ethylene: Gaseous Signaling, Ripening and Senescence
word_count_method: Whitespace-separated tokens in p.teaching-prose elements after stripping markup; article estimate excludes SVG, includes headings, tables, questions, and references.
comparison: Adjacent 6.D.10 internal QA reports 14,369 lexical narrative words, 17 sections, 50 explained questions; 6.D.08 is comparable in breadth and narrative depth (counts use slightly different methods).
coverage: Ethylene chemistry and gas movement; ACS/ACO and oxygen dependence; Yang cycle and ACC transport/conjugation; ER receptors, CTR1, EIN2, EIN3/EIL and feedback; mutant epistasis and triple response; dose and chamber flux calculations; climacteric and nonclimacteric ripening; abscission and floral senescence; flooding, rice strategies and hormonal crosstalk. Syllabus mapping retained from draft.
review: Prior draft internally rated 94. This pass independently checked biosynthetic and receptor logic against Van de Poel et al. review (PMID 32790878), Schaller et al. ethylene signaling review (PMID 32332098), Ju et al. (PMID 23132950), Qiao et al. (PMID 22936567), Roman et al. (PMID 7768447), ETR1 loss-of-function (PMID 12177468), 1-MCP meta-analysis (PMID 33328458) and nonclimacteric review (PMC11082881). Expanded 16 question explanations with mechanism and distractor analysis; improved all diagram zoom button names and added focus return.
score_basis: Internal self-assessment; assessment raised from 9 to 10 following substantive rationales across 16 previously less developed questions. Browser/technical deductions retained.
limitations: Internal self-assessment, not independent peer review.
Full browser/mobile/keyboard and all reference reachability tests not completed; local runtime cannot resolve raw.githubusercontent.com. Accessibility and technical deductions retained.
